thread:
maya: Quick sanity check — we need a tiny contract doc for how runtime signals rate limits per-endpoint and for bursts. I'm updating the SDK guidance but want to make sure ops/runtime agreed semantics.
aj: For compatibility, stick with standard headers where possible (`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`). For per-route context include a separate header like `X-RateLimit-Route` or `X-Route-ID`. SDKs can parse that if present.
sam: Couple questions: 1) how do we differentiate a transient/burst soft limit vs a hard reject? 2) should soft-degrades return 200 with a warning or still use 429?
maya: good Qs. My proposal: keep 429 as the canonical client-facing backpressure. For soft degradations we can either return a 200 with `X-RateLimit-Soft-Warning: reason` OR return a 429 with `x-rate-limit-soft: 1` — but mixing is confusing. leaning to always 429 so clients implement one branch.
aj: I agree: one branch is simpler. Use 429 for both hard and soft, but surface subtype in the response body and headers so clients know whether to retry immediately or back off longer.
karen: ops perspective: prefer `Retry-After` for hard enforced throttles (seconds or HTTP-date) and `X-RateLimit-Backoff: soft|hard` for hinting. Also include `X-RateLimit-Bucket` or `X-Quota-Bucket` so we can correlate across routes.
sam: OK. Example shapes would help — can we land on a JSON body for 429? Something like:
```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limited",
    "subtype": "burst",
    "retry_after": 1.2,
    "bucket": "org:123:route:/v1/generate"
  }
}
```
maya: that looks good. I'll add a short note that `retry_after` is seconds as a float and SDKs should fall back to `Retry-After` header if present (RFC 7231 formats).
aj: minor: prefer header names be lowercase in examples for consistency but it's fine. Also clarify semantics when `X-RateLimit-Remaining` goes negative for bursts vs when it stays >=0. Suggest we document that runtime may allow temporary negative remaining to handle burst windows and still emit 429 when threshold crossed.
karen: runtime note — we will emit `X-RateLimit-Remaining` which may briefly be negative; `X-RateLimit-Reset` points to the epoch when the bucket refills. For per-route accounting we also emit `X-RateLimit-Route: /v1/generate:default`.
sam: fallback behavior question: if primary model route is over quota and there is a compatible cheaper variant, will runtime automatically fallback or will clients see 429? @deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: runtime info: if a fallback policy is configured for the route, runtime will attempt fallback to a compatible variant and will return `X-RateLimit-Fallback: <variant-id>` when a fallback is used. If no fallback available, the client will receive 429 as usual. Fallbacks count against their own buckets and will emit their own rate headers.
aj: perfect — that addresses a lot. One more: SDKs should parse both `Retry-After` (header) and `error.retry_after` (body) and prefer header if both present. Also support parsing RFC7231 timestamp strings.
maya: got it. I'll draft the tiny contract doc with: header list, 429 body schema, per-route header examples, and fallback note. I'll include a short example for node/python SDK parse logic. Will send PR to `docs/api/rate-limits.md` and ping here when ready.
sam: thanks, this is actionable. ping me for review.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
aj: +1
karen: +1
